# ADR-050 — CHECK constraints only on project-controlled, closed vocabularies; provider-defined vocabularies are Zod-enforced

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**CHECK constraints only on vocabularies this project fully controls and that are closed by design.** `status`, `backfill_status`, sync-run `kind`/`status`, `external_key_source` and structural invariants (including all-or-nothing completeness of every encrypted credential triple) are CHECKed. `provider`, `metric`, `source_family` and `failure_class` are **not** — they are provider-defined or expected to grow, and are Zod-enforced instead. The reason is concrete and local: `packages/db/scripts/reconcile-drizzle-tracking.ts` understands `ADD CONSTRAINT ... CHECK` but **not** `DROP CONSTRAINT`, so widening a CHECK later forces a hand-written, unreconcilable migration — which is exactly what `0009_caldav_provider_support.sql` did and exactly why that reconcile script had to be written. Adding a health metric or a second health provider must never require repeating that (Phase 6 Checkpoint 6.0, user-approved 2026-08-24)
